questiontext.text:
A question type for C write-a-function questions. The student answer is expected to be a complete C function, but it can optionally be preceded by other self-contained C code such as preprocessor directives and support functions.

The test code for such questions typically calls the student function with some test arguments and prints the result, such as

printf("%d\n", someIntFunction(blah1, blah2))

The test case's Expected field is the expected output from the test.

If there is no standard input supplied for any of the test cases, a single test program is constructed, consisting of:

  1. The following standard #includes: stdlib.h, ctype.h, string.h, stdbool.h, math.h
  2. The student answer.
  3. A sequence of blocks wrapped in braces for each of the given test cases. Each block contains just the test case's test code. There is also a printf statement added between code blocks to print a special separator that is used to split the output back into individual test case outputs.

However, if any of the test cases has non-empty standard input, multiple test programs are run, one for each test case.

The test case's extra field is ignored.

summary.text: C: the student writes one or more functions, called by each test.
